title: Phase 0 Interactivity Observability and Dependency Freeze
description:
Phase 0 of the Interactive Job Runtime Refactor (master ticket 26/08/20/INTERACTIVE-JOB-RUNTIME-REFACTOR).

Deliverables:
1. New framework module for interactivity tracing: UI-callback timers, worker-step timers, thread-ownership assertions, active-worker and permit counters, queue item/byte counters, operation/generation tracing, preview-latency and cancellation-latency tracing, watchdog primitives with an 8 ms hard ceiling.
2. Static forbidden-call audit wired into the repo verify pipeline via 📜️script.ts: flags block_on, run_blocking, and synchronous filesystem/network/clipboard/database calls reachable from UI modules. Warn-level in Phase 0, deny-level in Phase 3.
3. Dependency freeze check: CI rejects newly introduced third-party packages (Rust and JS) against a recorded baseline inventory.
4. Four inventories written into the master ticket folder: dependency inventory (crate -> users -> purpose -> replacement owner), interactive-command inventory across all plugins, thread/pool-creation census, non-suspending async fn census.

Exit gate: every input, frame, operation, preview and commit can be followed by id through a trace; all four inventories complete and machine-readable.
summary:
Phase 0 of the Interactive Job Runtime Refactor is complete; the exit gate is met.

Built:
- New zero-dependency framework module `semio-framework-trace` at 🧰️framework/🔨️modules/⏱️trace/ providing UI-callback and worker-step timers, an 8 ms hard ceiling with five soft targets, a non-panicking Watchdog recording queryable contract violations, per-site percentile rings, thread-role registration and assertions, lock-free worker/permit/queue counters, and an operation trace ring with preview-latency and cancellation-latency queries. Clock abstracted so native, wasm32-unknown-unknown and wasm32-wasip2 all build. Verified independently by the coordinator: cargo check exit 0, 12/12 tests.
- Static forbidden-call audit `bun ./📜️script.ts verify interactivity` (WARN now, one-line flip to DENY in Phase 3) covering block_on/run_blocking, synchronous filesystem/network/clipboard/process/database calls in UI-reachable roots, and thread/pool construction repo-wide outside the sanctioned runtime modules. First run: 180 findings (122 blocking-bridge, 36 sync-fs, 10 thread-pool, 6 clipboard, 6 process), 121 blocking-bridge findings not allow-listed.
- Dependency freeze ratchet `bun ./📜️script.ts verify dependencies` with committed baseline 🔒️dependencies.json (238 third-party deps: 134 JS, 104 Rust). Ratchet failure mode exercised, not just asserted.
- Both wired into project.json and launch.json following existing order, grouping and naming.

Inventories (in the master ticket folder):
- Async census: 53,338 classified async fn — 11.72% genuinely suspending, 1.66% A-shallow, 74.61% decorative-simple, 12.01% decorative long-running CPU work, 0 unparseable. 88.28% effectively non-suspending. 1,085 category-C functions in the FEM/Energy/Puzzle/WFC hot spots, top 100 ranked. Produced by a brace-matching tool with a 30/30 self-test, plus machine-readable JSON that will drive the later de-async codemod. This supersedes an earlier sampled estimate whose percentages summed to 112%.
- Command inventory: ~357 interactive commands across all plugins and framework-level operations, with cost, resumability, mutation/preview and I/O characteristics, plus a ranked 8 ms-budget risk list.
- Dependency inventory: all 238 entries with purpose, surface size, API-leak flags, replacement strategy, risk and owning phase. Verified unused count is ZERO; an earlier claim that criterion, neo4rs, rusqlite, spade and sqlx were unused was retracted after direct reference counts disproved it.
- Thread census: 28 creation sites; 15 deterministic threads on a 10-core native session plus unbounded ad-hoc threads; 5 sites need genuine restructuring; confirmed ThreadBudget::checkout wraps silently in release builds.

Findings that change the downstream plan: de-async must be an automated span-keyed codemod rather than hand edits; AGENTS.md:44 mandates the async style and must not be edited, so the narrowing to genuine-suspension-only is recorded in the ticket instead; Phase 1 scope grows to include ad-hoc DB/store-sync/submit/HTTP threads and a per-document embedded tokio runtime.
